takeaway: A null hypothesis is a statement of no significant difference or effect. Type I error: a false positive; Type II error: a false negative.

lines.text: In statistics, every study starts with a null hypothesis.
A null hypothesis is a statement of no significant difference, or no effect.
For example, no significant difference between two groups,
or no effect from a treatment.
A Type One error wrongly rejects a true null hypothesis: a false positive. A benefit is seen when there is none.
A Type Two error accepts a false null hypothesis: a false negative. A real benefit is missed.
And remember: sensitivity is the true positive rate, and specificity is the true negative rate.
